comms.summary: IMNN-001, an IL-12 DNA immunotherapy, is in the Phase 3 OVATION 3 study (500 patients, 1:1, primary endpoint OS) for newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer combined with neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy. Final Phase 2 OVATION 2 data showed a 14.7-month median OS improvement over standard-of-care chemotherapy (rising from prior 11.1 months), with a 24.2-month OS increase in patients also receiving PARP inhibitors.

Phase 1b MUIR trial (paclitaxel arm, n=46) in all-comer platinum-resistant ovarian cancer showed 39.1% ORR and 7.3-month median PFS versus historical paclitaxel monotherapy (~30% ORR, ~4 months); the 250 mg 5+2 intermittent cohort achieved 50% ORR and 9.2-month median DOR, identified as the potential optimal dose (December 1, 2025 cutoff, ASCO 2026). Activity was comparable in Cyclin E1-positive and -negative patients, and Zentalis's core focus remains registration-intended azenosertib monotherapy in Cyclin E1-positive PROC.

IMNN-001, a DNA-based IL-12 immunotherapy for newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer, is in the pivotal Phase 3 OVATION 3 trial (first patient dosed Q3 2025, enrollment expected complete by Q1 2029), with FDA aligned on the protocol and BLA path. Final Phase 2 OVATION 2 data (March 25, 2026) showed a 14.7-month median overall survival improvement (45.1 vs. 30.4 months), rising to 24.2 months with PARP-inhibitor maintenance.

Olvi-Vec (olvimulogene nanivacirepvec), Genelux's lead candidate, is a proprietary modified vaccinia virus (VACV) oncolytic immunotherapy delivered regionally (e.g., intraperitoneal), locally, or systemically for aggressive/difficult-to-treat tumors. The late clinical-stage company has no approved products or product revenue and reported a net loss of $8.9 million for Q1 2026.

Defactinib (a FAK inhibitor) is a component of Verastem's FDA-approved AVMAPKI FAKZYNJA CO-PACK (avutometinib plus defactinib) for adult patients with KRAS mutant recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer. The confirmatory Phase 3 RAMP 301 trial is intended to verify RAMP 201 results and potentially expand the indication regardless of KRAS mutation status; defactinib is licensed from Pfizer.

Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan) is a late-stage program Genmab is advancing toward key readouts and preparing for a potential launch, with Q1 2026 operating expenses rising partly due to its advancement and buildout of global commercialization capabilities. No specific clinical results, phase, or indication details are disclosed in these excerpts.

Phase 3 TALAPRO-3 (March 2026) topline results were positive: Talzenna plus Xtandi met its primary endpoint with a statistically significant, clinically meaningful improvement in radiographic progression-free survival versus placebo plus Xtandi in HRR gene-mutated metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, exceeding the pre-specified target HR of 0.63. Benefit was consistent across BRCA and non-BRCA HRR alterations, with no new safety signals.

Merck's investigational TROP2-directed ADC sac-TMT (MK-2870), licensed from Kelun-Biotech, is in Phase 3 across multiple tumors including bladder (entered April 2026), breast, cervical, endometrial, gastric, NSCLC, and ovarian, with Phase 2 in biliary, esophageal, and pancreatic. In October 2025, Blackstone agreed to fund $700 million of 2026 development costs in exchange for low-to-mid single-digit royalties contingent on U.S. approval in first-line triple-negative breast cancer (TroFuse-011).

A Phase 3 trial was initiated for sofetabart mipitecan in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation for the treatment of certain patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

Preclinical data show azenosertib (WEE1 inhibitor) has monotherapy antitumor activity across 12 TNBC CDX/PDX models—including niraparib/olaparib-resistant lines—supported by TNBC's high Cyclin E1 expression (95%) and TP53 loss (88%). Combining azenosertib with TOP1i-payload ADCs (sacituzumab govitecan, Dato-DXd, T-DXd) enhanced tumor growth inhibition (e.g., 103% vs. 28% TGI for T-DXd) and duration of response.

IMNN-001, an IL-12 DNA-mediated immunotherapy, is in the pivotal Phase 3 OVATION 3 trial for newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer, with enrollment reported ahead of plan. Final Phase 2 OVATION 2 data (March 25, 2026; n=112) showed a 14.7-month median overall survival benefit (45.1 vs. 30.4 months) added to standard chemotherapy, and 24.2 months (65.6 vs. 41.4) with PARP inhibitor maintenance.

Olvi-Vec (olvimulogene nanivacirepvec), Genelux's lead oncolytic vaccinia virus immunotherapy (LIVP strain; formerly GLV-1h68/GL-ONC1), is being evaluated to demonstrate platinum-resensitization across three trials: a U.S. Phase 3 registrational trial in platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer (PRROC), a U.S. Phase 2 in recurrent NSCLC, and a Phase 1b/2 in China for recurrent SCLC. Across seven completed early/mid-phase trials it was well tolerated with no maximum tolerated dose reached.

The Phase 3 confirmatory RAMP 301 trial is enrolling, and defactinib is also being tested with LUMAKRAS in KRAS G12C NSCLC (RAMP 203).

Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan, GEN1184), a folate receptor alpha–targeted TOPO1 ADC from the ProfoundBio acquisition, showed a confirmed 50.0% ORR (95% CI, 26.0–74.0) at 120 mg/m² Q3W in ovarian cancer patients regardless of FRα expression, with no ocular toxicity, neuropathy, or ILD (ESMO 2024). It holds FDA Fast Track for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, and a Phase 3 second-line-plus trial was expected to start by end-2024.

Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan, GEN1184), a folate receptor alpha–targeted TOPO1 ADC from the ProfoundBio acquisition, showed a confirmed 50.0% ORR (95% CI, 26.0–74.0) at 120 mg/m² Q3W in ovarian cancer patients regardless of FRα expression, with no ocular toxicity, neuropathy, or ILD (ESMO 2024). It holds FDA Fast Track for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, and a Phase 3 second-line-plus trial was expected to start by end-2024.

It holds FDA Fast Track for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, and a Phase 3 second-line-plus trial was expected to start by end-2024.
Pfizer transferred $727 million of talazoparib (Talzenna) from IPR&D to developed technology rights during the first nine months of 2024, reflecting the asset reaching commercial/approved status.

Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT), an anti-TROP2 ADC being developed in collaboration with Kelun-Biotech, had new positive investigational data presented at ESMO 2024. No specific trial, phase, or indication results are detailed in these excerpts.

Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT), an anti-TROP2 ADC being developed in collaboration with Kelun-Biotech, had new positive investigational data presented at ESMO 2024. No specific trial, phase, or indication results are detailed in these excerpts.

CHMP adopted a positive opinion recommending marketing authorization of Elahere (mirvetuximab soravtansine) for FRα-positive, platinum-resistant high-grade serous epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in patients who received one to three prior regimens, supported by the Phase 3 MIRASOL trial; EC decision expected later this year. AbbVie also presented full primary-analysis data from the single-arm Phase 2 PICCOLO trial at ESMO 2024.

INCB123667, a highly selective, potentially first-in-class CDK2 inhibitor, showed single-agent antitumor activity across doses in Phase 1, notably in ovarian and endometrial cancers overexpressing Cyclin E1 (CCNE1). Incyte plans to initiate a pivotal ovarian cancer trial in 2025, with combination Phase 1 studies ongoing.

Talazoparib (Talzenna), an oral PARP inhibitor, met its final prespecified overall survival endpoint in the Phase 3 TALAPRO-2 study when combined with Xtandi (enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (October 2024). It showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS improvement versus Xtandi alone in both all-comers and HRR gene-mutated patients.

Avutometinib + defactinib (RAF/MEK clamp plus FAK inhibitor) showed in the registration-directed Phase 2 ENGOT-ov60/GOG-3052/RAMP 201 primary analysis (data cutoff June 30, 2024) an ORR by blinded independent review in recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, with responses observed across both KRAS-mutant (n=58) and wild-type (n=57) patients. The combination previously received FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation (May 2021) based on the Phase 1 FRAME study.

The avutometinib/defactinib combination showed a confirmed ORR of 31% overall (44% KRAS mutant, 17% KRAS wild-type) with median PFS of 12.9 months (22 months in KRAS mutant) in recurrent LGSOC in Phase 2 RAMP 201, with a 10% AE discontinuation rate. Verastem is on track to complete an NDA submission in October 2024 seeking Accelerated Approval for recurrent KRAS mutant LGSOC, targeting the U.S. market in 2025.

Phase 2 OVATION 2 Study in first-line advanced ovarian cancer reported positive topline results (July 30, 2024): IMNN-001 plus standard-of-care produced an 11.1-month median OS increase in ITT (HR 0.74), with PFS improvement of ~3 months (HR 0.79); PARP-inhibitor subgroup HR fell to 0.41. The company plans an End-of-Phase 2 FDA meeting and a Phase 3 pivotal study anticipated to begin Q1 2025.

IMNN-001, Imunon's lead program, is a TheraPlas DNA-based immunotherapy in Phase II development for localized treatment of advanced ovarian cancer, designed to produce durable levels of IL-12 and interferon gamma at the tumor site. It is being developed as an addition to platinum-based first-line chemotherapy for a disease with high recurrence rates and poor five-year survival.

Talazoparib (Talzenna) reached a regulatory/commercial milestone, triggering the transfer of $727 million from in-process R&D to developed technology rights (i.e., product approval/launch). No clinical trial data or indication specifics are disclosed in these excerpts.

Phase 3 data from a China-based study (led by partner Kelun-Biotech) of sacituzumab tirumotecan (MK-2870/SKB264), an investigational anti-TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate, were presented at ASCO 2024 in previously treated patients with locally recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

Phase 3 data from a China-based study (led by partner Kelun-Biotech) of sacituzumab tirumotecan (MK-2870/SKB264), an investigational anti-TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate, were presented at ASCO 2024 in previously treated patients with locally recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

The Phase 2 OVATION 2 study of IMNN-001 (IL-12 immunotherapy) plus standard-of-care NACT in newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer showed an 11.1-month median OS increase in the ITT population (HR 0.74) and a 3-month PFS improvement (HR 0.79); benefit was greater with PARP inhibitors (HR 0.41). IMUNON plans an End-of-Phase 2 FDA meeting and a registrational Phase 3 study in Q1 2025.

Positive topline Phase 2 PICCOLO results for Elahere (mirvetuximab soravtansine) monotherapy in heavily pre-treated FRα-positive, platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer; the trial met its primary endpoint with an ORR of 51.9% and a median DOR of 8.25 months. The safety profile was consistent with prior studies, with no new safety concerns, and full data will be presented at a future medical meeting.

comms.description: IMFINZI APPROVED IN THE US FOR ENDOMETRIAL CANCER
comms.summary: In the Phase III DUO-E trial (GOG 3041/ENGOT-EN10) in 1st-line advanced/recurrent endometrial cancer, the Imfinzi plus Lynparza (olaparib) maintenance arm met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival, with OS continuing as a key secondary endpoint. Regulatory applications for the Imfinzi and Lynparza regimen are under review in the EU, Japan, and several other countries.

Olvi-Vec (olvimulogene nanivacirepvec), Genelux's most advanced candidate and a modified vaccinia virus strain, is being evaluated in OnPrime/GOG-3076, a multi-center, randomized, open-label Phase 3 registrational trial in platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer. The trial tests Olvi-Vec plus platinum-doublet + bevacizumab versus physician's choice of chemotherapy and bevacizumab.

Olvi-Vec (olvimulogene nanivacirepvec), Genelux's most advanced candidate and a modified vaccinia virus strain, is being evaluated in OnPrime/GOG-3076, a multi-center, randomized, open-label Phase 3 registrational trial in platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer, testing it plus platinum-doublet + bevacizumab versus physician's choice chemotherapy and bevacizumab. Topline results are anticipated with company funding runway extending through Q1 2026.

Avutometinib (RAF/MEK clamp), combined with defactinib (FAK inhibitor), is Verastem's lead program targeting low-grade serous ovarian cancer (LGSOC), with a rolling NDA submission planned for 2024 based on topline RAMP 201 data, potentially the first approved LGSOC therapy. Additional development includes RAMP 205 and RAMP 301 trials and combinations with LUMAKRAS.

Genmab acquired Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan), an FRα-targeting Topo1 ADC, via its USD 1.8 billion all-cash acquisition of ProfoundBio, completed May 21, 2024. The candidate is in part 2 of a Phase 1/2 trial for ovarian and other FRα-expressing solid tumors and received FDA Fast Track designation in January 2024 for FRα-expressing platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

The candidate is in part 2 of a Phase 1/2 trial for ovarian and other FRα-expressing solid tumors and received FDA Fast Track designation in January 2024 for FRα-expressing platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

The candidate is in part 2 of a Phase 1/2 trial for ovarian and other FRα-expressing solid tumors and received FDA Fast Track designation in January 2024 for FRα-expressing platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.
Talazoparib (Talzenna) reached commercialization, reflected by the transfer of $727 million of in-process R&D to developed technology rights during Q1 2024.

Azenosertib, Zentalis's lead WEE1 inhibitor, is being evaluated in 10+ trials across gynecological and solid tumors, with two registration-enabling Phase 2 monotherapy studies pending: DENALI in platinum-resistant high-grade serous ovarian cancer (topline 1H 2025) and TETON in uterine serous carcinoma (topline 2H 2025). The company targets its first NDA in a gynecologic malignancy in 2026, with Phase 1 osteosarcoma combination (gemcitabine) data presented at ASCO 2024.

Sacituzumab tirumotecan (MK-2870), a TROP2 ADC, is in Phase 3 across multiple indications: breast (entered April 2024), endometrial (December 2023), and non-small-cell lung (November 2023), with additional Phase 2 work in neoplasm malignant.

Sacituzumab tirumotecan (MK-2870), a TROP2 ADC, is in Phase 3 across multiple indications: breast (entered April 2024), endometrial (December 2023), and non-small-cell lung (November 2023), with additional Phase 2 work in neoplasm malignant.

INCB123667, a selective CDK2 inhibitor, showed early clinical activity in a Phase 1 study for solid tumors, with several partial responses in patients with CCNE1 amplification/overexpression (a potential predictive biomarker) and tumor shrinkage across multiple types including CCNE1+ ovarian cancer. The safety profile aligned with its mechanism of action, and additional data was expected in 2024.

AbbVie added Elahere (mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx), an antibody-drug conjugate, via its completed acquisition of ImmunoGen for FRα-positive, platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. The FDA granted full approval for FRα-positive platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer (up to three prior therapies), based on the confirmatory MIRASOL Phase 3 trial showing an overall survival benefit and 35% reduction in progression risk.

Genmab is acquiring ProfoundBio for USD 1.8 billion in cash (expected to close H1 2024) to gain worldwide rights to Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan/PRO1184), a next-generation FRα-targeted Topo1 ADC currently in Phase 2 of a Phase 1/2 trial for ovarian cancer and other FRα-expressing solid tumors. The FDA granted Fast Track designation in January 2024 for FRα-expressing high-grade serous or endometrioid platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

Genmab is acquiring ProfoundBio for USD 1.8 billion in cash (expected to close H1 2024) to gain worldwide rights to Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan/PRO1184), a next-generation FRα-targeted Topo1 ADC currently in Phase 2 of a Phase 1/2 trial for ovarian cancer and other FRα-expressing solid tumors. The FDA granted Fast Track designation in January 2024 for FRα-expressing high-grade serous or endometrioid platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

Genmab is acquiring ProfoundBio for USD 1.8 billion in cash (expected to close H1 2024) to gain worldwide rights to Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan/PRO1184), a next-generation FRα-targeted Topo1 ADC currently in Phase 2 of a Phase 1/2 trial for ovarian cancer and other FRα-expressing solid tumors. The FDA granted Fast Track designation in January 2024 for FRα-expressing high-grade serous or endometrioid platinum-resistant ovarian cancer.

Olvi-Vec (olvimulogene nanivacirepvec; formerly GLV-1h68/GL-ONC1), Genelux's lead candidate, is a genetically attenuated Lister-strain vaccinia virus oncolytic immunotherapy being developed across multiple solid tumors via regional, local, and systemic delivery, as monotherapy and in combination. It has been studied in ~150 patients across seven early/mid-phase trials, was well tolerated with no MTD reached; Genelux licensed China rights to Newsoara in September 2021.
AZD5335, an FRα-targeting ADC, advanced into the clinic in 2023, demonstrating the strength of AstraZeneca's proprietary ADC technology.

INCB123667, Incyte's selective small-molecule CDK2 inhibitor, showed promising early Phase 1 efficacy (January 2024) with several partial responses in patients with CCNE1 amplification/overexpression and tumor shrinkage across multiple tumor types, including CCNE1+ ovarian cancer. The safety profile aligned with its mechanism of action, and additional data is expected in 2024.

AbbVie acquired ImmunoGen (completed February 12, 2024; $31.26/share) primarily for ELAHERE (mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx), the first FDA-approved ADC in ovarian cancer, granted accelerated approval for FRα-positive, platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in patients with one to three prior regimens. A confirmatory trial under FDA review reportedly shows ELAHERE is the first targeted agent to offer a survival benefit in PROC, supporting label-expansion into earlier lines; the label carries a boxed warning for ocular toxicities.

AbbVie will acquire ImmunoGen and its flagship therapy Elahere (mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx), a first-in-class antibody-drug conjugate approved for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, in a deal valuing ImmunoGen at approximately $10.1 billion. The acquisition accelerates AbbVie's entry into the solid tumor space.

Verastem plans to begin a rolling NDA submission for accelerated approval of avutometinib (RAF/MEK clamp) plus defactinib in recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer in H1 2024, targeting a potential 2025 launch; the combination holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation and showed a 45% ORR (13/29) in the Phase 1/2 RAMP 201 trial. It is also being studied in KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC (RAMP 203/204, with sotorasib/adagrasib) and frontline metastatic pancreatic cancer (RAMP 205), with a confirmatory Phase 3 RAMP 301 trial underway in LGSOC.

Azenosertib (ZN-c3), Zentalis's lead candidate, is a potentially first-in-class/best-in-class WEE1 inhibitor being developed for advanced solid tumors and hematologic malignancies, evaluated as monotherapy and in chemotherapy combinations across multiple trials with a focus on ovarian cancer. The company reports it has been well tolerated with single-agent anti-tumor activity, and is pursuing enrichment strategies targeting Cyclin E1-positive and homologous recombination-deficient tumors.
Mentioned in passing.

AbbVie will acquire ImmunoGen for ~$10.1 billion ($31.26/share cash, expected to close mid-2024), gaining flagship ADC ELAHERE (mirvetuximab soravtansine-gynx), a first-in-class folate receptor-alpha–targeting ADC with accelerated FDA approval for FRα-positive platinum-resistant ovarian cancer after one to three prior regimens. Late-stage programs aim to expand into earlier lines of therapy; the label carries a boxed warning for severe ocular toxicities.

Verastem plans to submit a U.S. accelerated approval application in H1 2024 for defactinib combined with avutometinib in recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer (LGSOC), based on the Phase 2 RAMP 201 trial; the confirmatory Phase 3 RAMP 301 trial (~270 patients vs. standard of care) was set to begin enrollment in Q4 2023. RAMP 201 subgroup data showed ORR of ~43.5% (10/23) even in patients who had poorly responded to prior therapy.

Azenosertib is Zentalis's first-in-class WEE1 inhibitor with global commercial rights and composition-of-matter IP to 2039, targeting ovarian cancer and uterine serous carcinoma (USC); monotherapy RP2D established at 400 mg on a 5:2 intermittent schedule, showing 37% ORR with durable responses and no treatment-related discontinuations. A Phase 3 trial in Cyclin E1+ platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer plus chemotherapy is slated to initiate Q1 2024, with USC holding FDA Fast Track designation.

Defactinib, Verastem's FAK inhibitor, is being developed in combination with the RAF/MEK inhibitor avutometinib across solid tumors including low-grade serous ovarian cancer (the lead registration-directed indication), NSCLC, colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, and melanoma. The combination is Verastem's most advanced program, with an ongoing registration-directed trial in LGSOC.

Zentalis announced the monotherapy RP2D for azenosertib, its potentially first-in-class WEE1 inhibitor, at 400 mg QD on a 5:2 intermittent weekly schedule (June 6, 2023). Intermittent dosing achieved a confirmed ORR of 36.8% (7/19) in combined ovarian/USC subgroups versus 19.2% on continuous dosing, with improved tolerability; three Phase 2 monotherapy trials are enrolling at the RP2D.

Positive Phase 1b data in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer showed the WEE1 inhibitor azenosertib plus paclitaxel achieved a confirmed ORR of 50.0% (mPFS 7.4m) and plus carboplatin an ORR of 35.7% (mPFS 10.4m), with Cyclin E1+ patients benefiting most (ORR 40.0% vs 8.3%). Zentalis plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial with intermittent dosing plus chemotherapy in Cyclin E1+ platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer in Q1 2024.

comms.description: ODAC VOTE ON LYNPARZA COMBO IN PROSTATE CANCER
comms.summary: FDA's ODAC voted 11-1 (1 abstaining) on 2 May 2023 that Lynparza (olaparib) plus abiraterone for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer should be limited to BRCA-mutated patients, rather than the broader all-comers population supported by the PROpel Phase III trial (based on rPFS). AstraZeneca and MSD will continue working with the FDA as it completes review of the sNDA accepted August 2022.

INCB123667, a selective oral CDK2 inhibitor, is in a Phase 1 trial for advanced malignancies including CCNE1-high TNBC and HR+/HER2- tumors post-CDK4/6 inhibitors. At AACR 2023, Incyte presented data showing significant single-agent activity in CCNE1-high breast cancer xenograft and patient-derived xenograft models.

The Phase 3 TALAPRO-2 study (February 2023) showed Talzenna (talazoparib), an oral PARP inhibitor, combined with Xtandi significantly improved radiographic progression-free survival versus placebo plus Xtandi in men with mCRPC, with or without HRR gene mutations. The FDA granted priority review for the combination sNDA with a decision expected in 2023, and the EMA accepted the corresponding MAA.

Zentalis will present positive Phase 1b data at ASCO (June 5, 2023) for its potentially first-in-class Wee1 inhibitor azenosertib combined with chemotherapy in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, supporting Cyclin E1 expression as a predictive marker. The company also announced Foundation Medicine and Roche Diagnostics collaborations to develop companion diagnostics identifying Cyclin E1-driven patients.

Azenosertib (ZN-c3), Zentalis's lead Wee1 inhibitor positioned as potentially first-/best-in-class, holds FDA Fast Track designation in uterine serous carcinoma and is being developed as monotherapy in biomarker-enriched populations (USC, Cyclin E1-driven, post-PARP) plus multiple combinations. Key near-term catalysts include a monotherapy RP2D/dosing update in 1H 2023 and Phase 1 dose-escalation results in ovarian cancer plus chemotherapy backbones in 1H 2023.

comms.description: LYNPARZA + IMFINZI MET ENDPOINT IN OVARIAN CANCER
comms.summary: The DUO-O Phase III interim analysis showed Lynparza (olaparib) combined with Imfinzi, chemotherapy and bevacizumab, followed by Imfinzi/Lynparza/bevacizumab maintenance, delivered a statistically significant and clinically meaningful PFS improvement versus chemotherapy plus bevacizumab in newly diagnosed advanced high-grade epithelial ovarian cancer patients without tumour BRCA mutations (announced 5 April 2023). Overall survival and other secondary endpoints remain immature and will be assessed at a subsequent analysis.

Olvi-Vec (olvimulogene nanivacirepvec), Genelux's lead oncolytic vaccinia virus immunotherapy, met the pre-established endpoint in its Phase 2 trial for platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer (PRROC). It is administered via regional, local, or systemic routes and is being developed as an off-the-shelf personalized immunotherapy across multiple solid tumor types.

Talazoparib is listed among Pfizer's in-line precision medicine/breast cancer assets in the context of the Seagen acquisition portfolio overview. No specific clinical, regulatory, or competitive detail is provided beyond this categorization.

Avutometinib (VS-6766), a RAF/MEK clamp, holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation in combination with defactinib for recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer (regardless of KRAS status) after one or more prior lines of therapy, and is in the registration-directed RAMP 201 trial. Additional trials evaluate avutometinib in KRAS-driven tumors, including combinations with LUMAKRAS and KRAZATI in KRAS G12C NSCLC (RAMP 203/204) and with chemotherapy in front-line metastatic pancreatic cancer (RAMP 205).

Defactinib, Verastem's FAK inhibitor, is being investigated in combination with avutometinib (VS-6766), a RAF/MEK inhibitor, across solid tumors including low-grade serous ovarian cancer, NSCLC, colorectal, pancreatic, uveal melanoma, and endometrial cancer. The company has an ongoing registration-directed trial for the combination.

comms.description: LYNPARZA APPROVED IN CHINA FOR OVARIAN CANCER
comms.summary: Lynparza (olaparib) was approved in China (22 September 2022) as 1st-line maintenance treatment with bevacizumab for HRD-positive advanced ovarian cancer, based on the PAOLA-1 Phase III trial. In the HRD-positive subgroup, the combination reduced risk of death by 38% (HR 0.62) versus bevacizumab alone and improved median PFS to 46.8 versus 17.6 months.

comms.description: LYNPARZA APPROVED IN JAPAN FOR EARLY BREAST CANCER
comms.summary: Lynparza (olaparib) was approved in Japan on 25 August 2022 as adjuvant treatment for BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer, making it the first and only approved medicine targeting BRCA mutations in this setting. Approval was based on the OlympiA Phase III trial, which showed a 42% reduction in invasive disease-free survival events (HR 0.58) and a 32% reduction in risk of death (HR 0.68, p=0.009) versus placebo.

comms.description: LYNPARZA APPROVED IN EU FOR EARLY BREAST CANCER
comms.summary: Lynparza (olaparib) was approved in the EU on 4 August 2022 as adjuvant monotherapy or with endocrine therapy for gBRCA-mutated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer, becoming the first PARP inhibitor in this setting. Approval was based on the OlympiA Phase III trial, which showed a 42% reduction in invasive disease-free survival events (HR 0.58) and 32% reduced risk of death (HR 0.68, p=0.009) versus placebo.

INCB123667 is a novel, potent, selective oral small-molecule CDK2 inhibitor that has suppressed tumor growth as monotherapy and combined with standard of care in Cyclin E–amplified tumor models. A Phase 1 dose-escalation and dose-expansion study in adults with selected advanced or metastatic solid tumors has been initiated.

comms.description: LYNPARZA RECOMMENDED IN EU FOR EARLY BREAST CANCER
comms.summary: Lynparza (olaparib), AstraZeneca/MSD's PARP inhibitor, received a positive CHMP opinion on 27 June 2022 for EU adjuvant treatment of gBRCAm, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer, based on OlympiA Phase III data showing a 42% reduction in invasive disease recurrence (HR 0.58) and 32% reduction in death (HR 0.68, p=0.009). It was already approved for this indication in the US in March 2022.

INCB123667 is a novel, potent, selective oral small-molecule CDK2 inhibitor shown to suppress tumor growth as monotherapy and combined with standard of care in Cyclin E-amplified tumor models in vivo. Incyte is initiating a Phase 1 dose-escalation/dose-expansion study in adults with selected advanced or metastatic solid tumors.

comms.description: LYNPARZA APPROVED IN US FOR EARLY BREAST CANCER
comms.summary: Lynparza (olaparib) was approved by the FDA on 14 March 2022 as adjuvant treatment for germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer following chemotherapy, becoming the first medicine targeting BRCA mutations in this setting. Approval was based on the OlympiA Phase III trial, which showed a 42% reduction in invasive disease-free survival risk (HR 0.58) and a 32% reduction in death risk (HR 0.68, p=0.0091) versus placebo.

comms.description: LYNPARZA COMBO DELAYS PROGRESSION RISK IN PROSTATE
comms.summary: Positive PROpel Phase III results (reported 15 Feb 2022, presented at ASCO GU) showed Lynparza (olaparib) plus abiraterone reduced risk of radiographic disease progression by 34% versus abiraterone alone as 1st-line treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, irrespective of HRR gene mutation status, delaying progression by more than eight months. Lynparza is already approved across multiple PARP-dependent tumor types including ovarian, breast, and pancreatic cancers.

In June 2021, Pfizer dosed the first participant in the Phase 3 TALAPRO-3 study evaluating talazoparib (marketed as Talzenna, an oral PARP inhibitor) combined with enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in men with DDR-deficient metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. Anticipated primary completion is late-2024.

comms.description: LYNPARZA REDUCED RECURRENCE RISK IN BREAST CANCER
comms.summary: Lynparza (olaparib) met its primary endpoint in the OlympiA Phase III trial, reducing the risk of cancer recurrence by 42% (invasive disease-free survival) versus placebo in adjuvant treatment of germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer; results were published in NEJM and presented at ASCO on 6 June 2021. It is the first medicine targeting BRCA mutations to show clinical benefit in the adjuvant setting, with AstraZeneca and MSD pursuing regulatory approval.

Defactinib (FAK inhibitor) is being developed in combination with VS-6766 (RAF/MEK inhibitor) across multiple RAS-mutant cancers; a recommended phase 2 dose was established for the doublet, with registration-directed RAMP phase 2 studies initiated in recurrent LGSOC (Nov 2020) and KRAS-mutant NSCLC (Dec 2020). Additional FRAME-study combinations are ongoing in CRC, pancreatic, endometrial cancers, and uveal melanoma.
